title: Mississippi and Alaska Senate Races Remain Uncalled as Counting Continues
dek: The AP had not called two close Senate contests by midday Wednesday. Mississippi's race is within a few dozen votes, and Alaska's could go to ranked-choice tabulation.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: As of noon Eastern on Wednesday, the Associated Press had not called a handful of Senate and governor races, while Democrats had already secured control of both chambers of Congress.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom led Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by a few dozen votes. Mississippi has no automatic recount, but a challenger can seek a court-ordered one.
In Alaska, the AP had not called the Senate contest between Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola, who led by 626 votes with an estimated 74% of the vote counted.
Under Alaska law, if no candidate tops 50%, the race goes to ranked-choice tabulation.
The AP said that in the House, 59 races where party control is at stake had not been called as of noon Wednesday.
body:
Most of the 2026 midterm results are settled, but several close races remain open. As of noon Eastern on Wednesday, the Associated Press had not called a handful of Senate and governor contests, according to the AP.

## Mississippi

In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom had a lead of a few dozen votes over Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the AP reported. The AP does not make projections and will call a race only when no scenario allows the trailing candidate to close the gap. Mississippi does not have an automatic recount process. A challenger can seek a court order for one.

## Alaska

The AP also had not called the Alaska Senate race between Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola. Peltola led by 626 votes with an estimated 74% of the vote counted. Under Alaska law, if neither candidate receives more than 50%, the race goes to ranked-choice tabulation.

## House

The AP reported that 59 House races in which party control is at stake had not been called as of noon Wednesday. The reporting reviewed for this story does not give a final House seat total.

## Why the calls are slow

The AP's policy is to call a race only when no remaining vote count could change the outcome. That is why the Mississippi race, with a lead of a few dozen votes, is still open. Close margins can narrow or widen as provisional and mail ballots are counted, and the AP's status can change within hours.

In Alaska, the ranked-choice step adds another layer. If neither Sullivan nor Peltola reaches 50% of first-choice votes, the tabulation redistributes votes from the lowest-ranked candidates until one candidate has a majority. The reporting reviewed for this story does not give a date for that process.

The Senate control result is already settled in the reporting reviewed for this story: Democrats won control of the chamber. The two open races could change the size of the Democratic majority, not which party controls the Senate.

## What is not yet known

The final outcome of the Mississippi and Alaska Senate races, and the number of uncalled House races, may change as remaining votes are counted. Meridian will update this story when the AP makes a call or official totals are reported.
